title: HomeGuard Homeowners Policy Roof Tear-Off and Disposal Allowance by Roof Material
content:
Under the HomeGuard Homeowners Policy, a re-settled wind or hail roof surfacing loss, one that stood on the claim only as a below-deductible denial, carries a tear-off and disposal allowance at a percentage of the roof surfacing's replacement-cost value. The percentage depends on the roof material on the declarations and, for asphalt, on the size of the loss.

## Allowance table

| Roof material on the declarations | Roof surfacing replacement-cost value | Allowance |
|---|---|---|
| Wood shake | Any | 8 percent |
| Tile/slate | Any | 8 percent |
| Asphalt, three-tab or architectural | 10000.00 or more | 5 percent |
| Asphalt, three-tab or architectural | Below 10000.00 | None: repaired in sections without a full tear-off |
| Metal | Any | None: overlaid or salvaged |

The replacement-cost value compared with 10000.00, and on which the percentage is taken, is the one recorded on the roof surfacing's below-deductible denial entry. The allowance is added to the reversal payment before the payment is floored at 0.00 and rounded to the cent once.

## Input, judgement, result

- **Input**: roof material; roof surfacing replacement-cost value on the denial entry.
- **Judgement**: is the material wood shake or tile/slate? If so, 8 percent. If it is asphalt of either kind, is the value at least 10000.00? If so, 5 percent. Metal, or asphalt below 10000.00: no allowance.
- **Result**: the allowance in dollars is the percentage multiplied by that replacement-cost value.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical figures)

- Architectural asphalt, replacement-cost value exactly 10000.00: 5 percent, 500.00.
- Three-tab asphalt, replacement-cost value 9999.99: no allowance.
- Tile/slate, replacement-cost value 6000.00: 8 percent, 480.00. For wood shake and tile/slate the size of the loss plays no part.
- Metal, replacement-cost value 30000.00: no allowance.
